content: Do not take enalapril if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately, as enalapril can harm the developing fetus. It is also used in combination with other drugs to manage heart failure. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. It works by reducing certain chemicals in the body that cause blood vessels to tighten, allowing blood to flow more easily and enabling the heart to pump blood more effectively. Enalapril is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once or twice daily, with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take enalapril exactly as prescribed; do not take more or less than directed or take it more frequently than instructed. Your doctor will likely start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Enalapril may also be used to treat kidney disease associated with diabetes. Discuss the potential risks and benefits of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. It may also be prescribed for other purposes; ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before starting enalapril, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to enalapril or any other ACE inhibitors, such as benazepril, captopril, fosinopril, lisinopril, moexipril, perindopril, quinapril, ramipril, or trandolapril. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Inform your doctor if you have a history of heart or kidney disease, lupus, scleroderma, diabetes, or angioedema (a condition causing swelling and difficulty breathing or swallowing). Let your doctor know if you are planning to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your surgeon or dentist that you are taking enalapril. Consult your doctor before using potassium-containing salt substitutes. If your doctor recommends a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of enalapril, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Enalapril may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they persist or worsen: cough, dizziness, rash, or weakness. Serious side effects are rare but require immediate medical attention. These include swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty breathing or swallowing; yellowing of the skin or eyes; fever, sore throat, chills, or other signs of infection; lightheadedness; or fainting. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store enalapril in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly; consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include lightheadedness or fainting. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments while taking enalapril. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Enalapril is sold under the brand names Vaseretic® and Vasotec®. Combination products containing enalapril include Lexxel®, which contains enalapril maleate and felodipine.
